content.title: About
content.content: Russian dressing is a thick sauce made from mayonnaise, tomato paste, horseradish, mustard and spices. It has a sweet‑tangy flavor with a mild kick and is commonly used as a dressing for salads, sandwiches and burgers.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The recipe is believed to have originated in the United States in the early 20th century as a milder alternative to the spicier Thousand Island dressing.
Traditional versions include finely chopped pickles or cornichons, giving the sauce its distinctive aroma.
Some variations replace part of the mayo with kefir or sour cream to lower the calorie count.
Russian dressing is often served with seafood, such as shrimp cocktail.
In Russia the sauce is sometimes called “Russian sauce,” although it has no direct connection to Russian cuisine.

items.title: Source of vitamin A
items.content: Tomato paste provides beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A, supporting vision.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: Mayonnaise supplies monounsaturated fatty acids that are beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Contains mustard
items.content: Mustard is rich in selenium and antioxidants that may help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Horseradish and vinegar stimulate gastric juice production, improving digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tomatoes and mustard provide vitamins B6 and B9, important for metabolism.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Mayonnaise contains eggs, which can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The sauce is relatively calorie‑dense due to mayo and added sugar, so it should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Salt and soy sauce in the recipe raise sodium levels, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

items.title: Spicy ingredients
items.content: Horseradish and mustard can irritate the stomach in people with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Russian dressing works well as a salad dressing (especially for Caesar or vegetable salads), as a sauce for burgers, sandwiches, wraps and seafood. It can also be used to marinate meat or as a dip for potato croquettes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the sauce in a sealed container in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C. Once opened, it is usually good for 1‑2 weeks. Discard if you notice off‑odors, color changes or mold.
